title: §28-002: Event Loop Lag Monitoring & Heap Profiling
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §28-002 (Event Loop Lag Monitoring & Heap Profiling).

cards.concept: Event Loop Lag Monitoring & Heap Profiling: OpenTelemetry Distributed Tracing
cards.question: How does OpenTelemetry correlate logs and spans across distributed microservices in a Node.js ecosystem?

options.text: By syncing server clocks using NTP down to the microsecond.
By propagating the standard `traceparent` header (Trace ID, Span ID, Trace Flags) across network requests and tracking execution context via `AsyncLocalStorage`.
By funneling all logs through a single shared socket.
By capturing screenshots of terminal output.

cards.explanation: OpenTelemetry injects the W3C Trace Context (traceparent header) into outbound HTTP/gRPC requests and uses AsyncLocalStorage to propagate context across asynchronous boundaries.
cards.pitfall: Failing to propagate context when dispatching background asynchronous jobs, breaking trace continuity.
cards.citation: W3C Trace Context Specification / OpenTelemetry Node.js SDK

cards.concept: Event Loop Lag Monitoring & Heap Profiling: Event Loop Delay Monitoring with perf_hooks
cards.question: How does Node's `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay()` measure event loop lag, and what does a high lag percentile indicate?

options.text: It measures network round-trip ping time to external DNS servers.
It samples timer execution delay against clock time using a high-resolution histogram; high lag percentiles indicate synchronous CPU-intensive tasks blocking the single thread.
It tracks operating system swap memory paging.
It measures disk read/write throughput in MB/s.

cards.explanation: monitorEventLoopDelay samples the time between timer checks and system clocks. If synchronous code blocks the event loop, timer callbacks are delayed, recorded as event loop delay.
cards.pitfall: Taking synchronous full V8 heap snapshots during peak production traffic freezes the event loop for seconds, triggering orchestrator healthcheck terminations.
